蘇州の日系部品メーカーで新規開拓を任された佐藤さんの一年半。電話一本から始まった: A year and a half in the life of Kenta Sato, tasked with finding new customers at a Japanese parts maker in Suzhou. Starting from a single phone call, his relationship with a client unfolds through complaints, contracts, negotiations, job interviews and banquet speeches, told in language you can use on the job in Chinese business.
新規のお客さんに電話で自己紹介: Introducing yourself to a new customer by phone
蘇州の日系精密部品メーカー「和成精密」の営業部に赴任して三か月の佐藤さん。上司の: Kenta Sato has been in the sales department of Hecheng Precision (「和成精密」), a Japanese precision parts maker in Suzhou, for three months. His boss, Director Yang, has handed him the cell phone number of Ms. Qian, purchasing manager at Ruida Electric (「瑞达电器」), a home appliance maker in Ningbo. The contact came through an industry acquaintance. At ten in the morning, with his materials laid out in front of him, he takes a deep breath and dials.
瑞达电器購買部のマネージャー、三十代後半。いつも忙しく、話は要点から聞きたいタイ: Purchasing manager at Ruida Electric, in her late thirties. Always busy, and wants to hear the main point first
和成精密営業部の日本人社員、三十二歳。蘇州に赴任して三か月。新規開拓を任されたば: Japanese employee in Hecheng Precision's sales department, 32. Three months into his posting in Suzhou, and just put in charge of finding new customers
初めて話す取引先候補。相手はこちらを知らないので、最初の三十秒で「誰が、誰の紹介: A prospective client you're speaking to for the first time. She doesn't know you, so the first thirty seconds are everything: say who you are, who referred you and why you're calling. Be polite with 「您」, but skip long, roundabout preambles and keep the conversation moving.
お世話になります。瑞达电器の钱マネージャーでいらっしゃいますか。: Hello! Is this Manager Qian of Ruida Electric?
中国の携帯電話は、出る側が名乗らず「喂」だけのことがほとんど。かける側が「请问是: In China, the person answering a cell phone almost never gives their name; they usually just say 「喂」. The caller confirms who they're speaking to with 「请问是...吗？」. The basic way to address someone is "surname + 「经理」". For purchasing staff, calling someone 「经理」 is never rude, even if they're only at section-chief level.
「您哪位？」は「どちら様ですか」。自分が聞くときも「你是谁？」は直接的すぎるので: 「您哪位？」 means "Who's calling?" When you ask this yourself, 「你是谁？」 is too blunt, so on the phone use 「请问您是哪位？」.
钱マネージャー、はじめまして。蘇州の和成精密の佐藤と申します。宏达機電の林社長の: Hello, Manager Qian. This is Sato from Hecheng Precision in Suzhou. Mr. Lin of Hongda Electromechanical suggested I get in touch with you.
紹介者がいるなら、名乗った直後に言うのが鉄則。中国のビジネスでは人のつながり（关: If someone referred you, the golden rule is to mention them right after giving your name. Personal connections (「关系」) matter a great deal in Chinese business, and just saying "So-and-so referred me" goes a long way toward lowering the other person's guard. The 「是...的」 in 「是……介绍我……的」 emphasizes who made the referral.
ああ、林さんから聞いてます。御社は何を作っている会社なんですか。: Oh, Mr. Lin mentioned you. What does your company do?
当社は日系企業で、主に精密プレス部品を作っています。たとえばモーターのブラケット: We're a Japanese-owned company, mainly making precision stamped parts, such as motor brackets and all kinds of small metal components.
「日资企业」は日系企業。口語では「日企」とも言います。「做〜」は「〜を作る／扱う: 「日资企业」 means a Japanese-owned company; in speech it's also shortened to 「日企」. 「做...」 means "to make / to deal in," and this one sentence is all you need to describe your line of business. If you launch into details right away, a busy listener will want to hang up.
そういうものは、うちはもう取引先がいますけどね。: We already have suppliers for that kind of thing, though.
承知しております。当社の強みは精度の高さと、納期が安定していることです。二分だけ: I understand. Our strengths are high precision and reliable delivery times. Could I take two minutes of your time to give you a quick introduction?
「已经有供应商了」は購買担当の決まり文句で、本気で断っているとは限りません。「明: 「已经有供应商了」 is a stock phrase for purchasing staff, and it doesn't necessarily mean a real no. The trick is to acknowledge it with 「明白」 and then state your strength in a word or two. 「占用您两分钟」 means "take two minutes of your time"; naming a specific, short amount of time makes it easier for the other person to say yes.
これからすぐ会議なんです。とりあえず資料を送ってください。: I'm about to go into a meeting. Send me your materials first.
かしこまりました。メールにお送りしましょうか。それともWeChatを追加させてい: Certainly. Should I send them to your email, or may I add you on WeChat?
中国では取引先とのやり取りも、メールよりWeChatが中心になることが多いです。: In China, even communication with business partners often happens mostly on WeChat rather than email. 「加一下您的微信」 is a polite way of saying "Let me add you on WeChat." Offering a choice with "A 「还是」 B?" lets the other person decide, so you don't come across as pushy.
WeChatでつながりましょう。この携帯番号がIDです。: Let's connect on WeChat. It's this phone number.
ありがとうございます、すぐ追加します。会社案内とサンプルの写真を、このあとすぐお: Great, I'll add you right away. I'll send you our company profile and photos of samples shortly.
わかりました。来月ちょうど蘇州でサプライヤーを何社か見て回る予定なので、そのとき: All right. As it happens, we're going to Suzhou next month to look at a few suppliers, so maybe we can stop by your place then.
ありがとうございます！ぜひ工場にお越しください。来週水曜の午前にあらためてお電話: That's wonderful! You're very welcome to visit our factory. May I call you again next Wednesday morning?
次の連絡の日時を自分から決めて確認するのが、営業電話の締め方。「再给您打个电话」: The way to wrap up a sales call is to propose the date and time of your next contact yourself and confirm it. The 「个」 in 「再给您打个电话」 is colloquial and keeps it light, giving it the soft feel of "give you a quick call."
いいですよ。じゃあ水曜にまた。: Sure. Let's talk again on Wednesday, then.
はい、お忙しいところ失礼いたしました。では、失礼します。: Thank you, and sorry to have taken up your time. Goodbye, Manager Qian!
「打扰您了」は「お邪魔しました、お時間を取らせました」。電話の最後に言うと、礼儀: 「打扰您了」 means "Sorry to have bothered you / to have taken your time." Saying it at the end of a call leaves a courteous impression. Putting the person's name and title before 「再见」 makes it even more polite.
電話の最初の確認に。「请问是〜吗？」＝〜さんでいらっしゃいますか: For confirming who you're speaking to at the start of a call. 「请问是...吗？」 = "Is this...?"
「您哪位？」＝どちら様？ 「谁」より丁寧: 「您哪位？」 = "Who's calling?" More polite than 「谁」
部長・課長クラスの呼び方。「钱经理」のように姓につける: Used to address people at department or section-head level. Attach it to the surname, as in 「钱经理」
「林总介绍我联系您」＝林社長の紹介でご連絡しました: 「林总介绍我联系您」 = "Mr. Lin suggested I contact you."
「再联系」＝また連絡します。「联系方式」＝連絡先: 「再联系」 = "Let's be in touch again." 「联系方式」 = contact details
略して「日企」。中国資本の会社は「中资企业」: Shortened to 「日企」. A Chinese-owned company is a 「中资企业」
「冲压」＝プレス加工。「零件」＝部品: 「冲压」 = stamping, press working. 「零件」 = part, component
買う側から見た取引先。顧客は「客户」: A business partner seen from the buyer's side. A customer is a 「客户」
「我们的优势是〜」で強みを一言で伝える: State your strength in a nutshell with 「我们的优势是...」
「交货期」の略。「交期稳定」＝納期が安定している: Short for 「交货期」. 「交期稳定」 = delivery times are reliable
「占用您几分钟」＝少しお時間をいただく: 「占用您几分钟」 = "take a few minutes of your time"
「先把资料发给我」＝まず資料を送って: 「先把资料发给我」 = "Send me the materials first."
「寄样品」＝サンプルを送る。「打样」＝試作する: 「寄样品」 = to send samples. 「打样」 = to make a prototype
「打扰您了」＝お時間を取らせました、失礼しました: 「打扰您了」 = "Sorry to have taken your time."
是 + 紹介者 + 介绍我 + 動詞 + 的: 是 + referrer + 介绍我 + verb + 的
「是〜的」は、すでに起きたことについて「誰が・いつ・どうやって」を強調する形。初: 「是...的」 emphasizes who, when or how for something that has already happened. It's handy for making clear that someone referred you when you call or visit for the first time. Be careful: if you leave out 「的」, it can sound as if the referral hasn't happened yet.
林社長のご紹介でご連絡しました。: Mr. Lin suggested I get in touch with you.
弊社の杨からお電話するよう言われまして。: Our Mr. Yang asked me to give you a call.
展示会で名刺をいただいた者です。: I got your business card at the trade show.
相手に選んでもらう疑問文。文末に「吗」はつけません。連絡方法や日時を決めるとき、: A question that lets the other person choose. Don't put 「吗」 at the end. When settling on a contact method or a date and time, offering two options yourself makes it easier for the other person to answer and keeps things moving.
メールにお送りしますか、それともWeChatがよろしいですか。: Should I send it to your email, or add you on WeChat?
水曜と木曜、どちらがご都合よろしいですか。: Which works better for you, Wednesday or Thursday?
……だけお時間をいただいて、……してもよろしいですか: Could I take... of your time to...?
能不能 + 占用您 + 時間 + ，+ したいこと + ？: 能不能 + 占用您 + amount of time + 「，」 + what you want to do + 「？」
忙しい相手に時間をもらうときの丁寧な頼み方。「两分钟」「十分钟」など具体的で短い: A polite way to ask a busy person for some of their time. The key is to name a specific, short amount of time, such as 「两分钟」 or 「十分钟」; it's easier for them to decide than if you just say "a moment." And always stick to the time you said.
二分ほどお時間をいただいて、簡単にご紹介してもよろしいですか。: Could I take about two minutes of your time to give you a quick introduction?
十分ほどお時間をいただいて、いくつか確認させていただけますか。: Could I take about ten minutes of your time to check a few things?
少しお時間よろしいでしょうか。: Could I have a moment of your time?
初めての取引先候補への電話、紹介を受けての連絡、展示会で名刺をもらった相手へのフ: Calling a prospective client for the first time, getting in touch after a referral, following up with someone whose card you got at a trade show. Ideally, go in this order: your name, your referrer, your business in a word, your strength, the next appointment, and finish in two or three minutes.
「お忙しいところ大変恐縮ですが、少々お時間を……」と前置きを重ねると、何の電話か: If you pile on preambles like "I'm terribly sorry to bother you when you're busy, but if I could have just a moment...," they won't know what the call is about and will hang up. And if you send materials without setting a date for the next contact, you will almost always be forgotten.
購買担当には毎日たくさんの営業電話がかかってきます。用件がはっきりしていて、相手: Purchasing staff get lots of sales calls every day. People who get straight to the point and respect the other person's time come across as competent. When a foreigner makes a real effort to speak Chinese, people are often surprisingly willing to hear them out.
中国のビジネスでは、知らない会社からの電話より、知っている人の紹介の方が圧倒的に: In Chinese business, a referral from someone they know carries far more weight than a call from an unknown company. That's why your referrer's name is your first and best weapon. Another characteristic is speed. Rather than talking at length on the phone, the norm is to swap WeChat contacts right away, send materials and photos, and move on with "Let's meet and talk in detail." Once you've connected on WeChat, sending a first message like 「您好，我是刚才给您打电话的和成精密的佐藤」 keeps you from getting buried in the other person's contact list.
電話の相手に「您哪位？」と聞かれました。この意味は？: On the phone, you're asked 「您哪位？」. What does it mean?
何名様ですか。: How many are in your party?
「您哪位？」は電話で相手の名前を尋ねる丁寧な言い方です。: 「您哪位？」 is a polite way to ask a caller's name on the phone.
紹介者がいることを伝える言い方として最も自然なのは？: Which is the most natural way to say that someone referred you?
すでに起きたことの「誰が」を強調するときは「是〜的」の形を使います。: To emphasize "who" for something that has already happened, use the 「是...的」 pattern.
「这些东西我们已经有供应商了」と言われました。まずどう返すのがいい？: You're told 「这些东西我们已经有供应商了」. What's the best first response?
まず受け止めて、自社の強みを短く伝えるのが基本。今の取引先を悪く言うのは逆効果で: The basic approach is to acknowledge it first, then briefly state your company's strengths. Speaking badly of their current supplier backfires.
電話の終わりに言う「打扰您了」の意味に近いのは？: Which is closest in meaning to 「打扰您了」 at the end of a call?
ご迷惑をおかけしております。: Sorry for all the trouble we're causing you.
お時間を取らせました、失礼いたしました。: Sorry for taking up your time.
「打扰您了」は相手の時間をもらったことへのお礼とおわびを込めた、電話の締めの言葉: 「打扰您了」 is a phrase for ending a call that combines thanks and an apology for taking up the other person's time.
